authorized_by: Control Tower directive H2O FULL CONTENT + MEDIA RECOVERY + REAL-STAGING VISUAL R2, sections 10-14
what_this_overlay_does_not_mean: NOT a change to any of the 68 frozen placements in MEDIA_PLACEMENT_AUTHORITY.tsv. That file is read, never written; all 68 rows still load, hash-verify and render.
NOT an alteration of any image binary. Every addition is placed at its recovered bytes; binary_altered is NO on every row and the loader still refuses a file whose sha256 does not match.
NOT an upscale. Every addition renders at or below the pixel width of its own crop window, which is itself a sub-rectangle of the native image.
NOT a project, customer, product-model or performance assertion. project_or_product_identity is NONE_ASSERTED on every row and every alt text describes only what the photograph shows.
NOT permission to index, publish or deploy.
why_this_overlay_exists: The 68 frozen placements are a preservation baseline: they prove selected files survived recovery correctly. They are not a statement that only 68 images exist, that they are the best available, or that the homepage should carry one 490px photograph. This overlay places ten further images that were already recovered into the same local stage and were classified AVAILABLE_NOT_SELECTED, and it records a presentation crop for each so a designed region can use a clean rectangle of the asset without touching the file.

crop_policy.rule: A crop is a fractional sub-rectangle of the native image, applied at render time with object-fit: cover and object-position. No derivative file is produced, no pixel is resampled at build time, and the binary on disk remains the recovered original at its recorded sha256.
crop_policy.why_a_crop_is_needed: Most recovered ICS imagery is a branded editorial slide: a real photograph with a headline, a logo badge or a URL bar composited over part of it. The photograph underneath is authentic and usable; the overlay is not. Cropping to the clean rectangle uses the evidence without reproducing a stale headline as site furniture, and without inventing a replacement image.
crop_policy.bounds: Each crop window is recorded as x0/y0/x1/y1 fractions plus the resulting pixel size. rendered_max_width_px never exceeds cropped_width, and cropped_width never exceeds native_width, so no upscaling is possible at either step.
crop_policy.what_a_crop_may_not_do: A crop may not remove or obscure a product label, model designation, manufacturer mark, dimension or technical configuration, and may not change the identity of any equipment shown. Every crop here removes composited marketing text and nothing else.

homepage_dominant_image_change.frozen_placement_retained: RT-0001 attachment 3452 remains a row of MEDIA_PLACEMENT_AUTHORITY.tsv, unchanged, and is still loaded and hash-verified.
homepage_dominant_image_change.reason: 3452 is 490x384 native, so it cannot drive a hero at any width without upscaling a frozen asset, and its own recorded alt text describes rooftop induced-draft cooling towers on a downtown building with a city skyline behind. That subject reads as commercial-building HVAC, which the directive excludes from ICS positioning. It is not deleted, altered or re-described; it is not shown on the homepage.

image_reuse_note: Two regions still share one binary: HOME_CAPABILITY_PARTS and PARTS_FEATURE both use attachment 19970, the fan hub photograph, at the same window. That is deliberate and it is a limitation, not a choice: 19970 is the only component close-up among the 145 images recovered to this machine, and the named component photography the inventory lists — the Tuf-Lite and FanStack hardware, the Brentwood fill range, the Amarillo and Addax drive components — exists as inventory rows with no bytes here. The duplicate is recorded rather than hidden.
